source_title: City's lord mayor-elect explains 'Hobart for Hobartians' slogan
source_excerpt:
Charles Wooley expressed surprise that women "didn't vote for women" in the election. ( ABC News: Greg Szabo )
Hobart's next lord mayor, Charles Wooley, has given his first press conference since being elected.
He secured the mayoral role with 55 per cent of the vote.
Counting is still continuing around the state, with many results for councillor and deputy mayor still to come.
Veteran journalist and author Charles Wooley fronted the cameras this morning, for the first time since being elected late yesterday as Hobart's next lord mayor.
In the wide-ranging media conference, Mr Wooley raised several topics including the Israel election, statues, Julius Caesar, Donald Trump, King Charles and museums. He also avoided several questions.
Mr Wooley's campaign slogan was "Hobart for Hobartians".
When asked what that meant, he said, "great question", before adding that the inspiration for it came from his travels in Barcelona in Spain, where he met that city's first female mayor.
"On the wall of her office she had 'Never forget for whom we run this city'," Mr Wooley said.
He was then asked what he thought about Hobart's council looking likely to only include one female councillor.
"Women didn't vote for women — it's extraordinary," he said.
As of 4:50pm yesterday, 50 per cent of the votes for Hobart councillor positions had been counted, with incumbent Louise Elliot the only female in the top nine.
Mr Wooley was asked how he was going to address the division within the Hobart City Council.
"By being nice," he replied. "The last eight years of council have been vitriolic. It's been terrible and I think partly because we had a mayor who thought she was the boss.
"I'm not the boss. I represent the council to you, to the public, and I will represent you, the public, to the council."
In terms of his key policy ideas for the next four years of council, he said, "one way or another I'm going to cap rates".
"My own inclination is to give everybody a $200 rate cut and say, 'go and spend it in town'.
"My advisers tell me I can't do that, but we'll see," he said.
Mr Wooley said he supported council amalgamations and wanted the local government code of conduct legislation reviewed.
"Almost everyone in Tasmania is sleeping with a politician or knows someone who is. It's silly," he said
Charles Wooley says he will address the division that has been plaguing Hobart City Council. ( ABC News: Greg Szabo )
Mr Wooley, who seemingly then forgot which side of the camera he was on — after many years of being the interviewer — then started asking the journalists questions.
"Let me ask some questions: do you own a house here? What is the budget of Hobart?"
Hobart Lord Mayor Anna Reynolds did not contest this election.
Several mayors across the state ran for re-election but were unsuccessful.
Teeny Brumby has been Burnie's mayor since 2023, but lost out this time around to her deputy, Giovanna Simpson.
"Naturally, I'm very disappointed not to have been returned as mayor. I've given this role absolutely everything," she said in a statement.
"I've often felt like a special ops warrior, dropped behind enemy lines to clear the slate and rebuild the foundations! We inherited a city facing enormous financial and organisational challenges.
"For those of us who haven't been returned, I think we also need to acknowledge the increasingly hostile environment in which elections are being contested."
Teeny Brumby says she is disappointed she was not returned as mayor. ( ABC News: Sandy Powell )
Clarence Mayor Brendan Blomeley was also not re-elected.
Newcomer Drew Jenner, who secured 51 per cent of the vote, will be the new mayor.
"I am proud of what we have achieved over this past term," Mr Blomeley said in a statement.
"I was humbled to receive the highest personal vote at this election, and I thank the community for their support and the opportunity to serve as their mayor."
Brendan Blomeley was unsuccessful in his bid to remain mayor of Clarence City Council. ( ABC News: Kate Nickels )
Shane Pitt also lost out to Lindsay Newman on the West Coast, and Michelle Dracoulis has been replaced by Casey Farrell in the Derwent Valley.
"It's very disappointing … I absolutely put everything into this," Ms Dracoulis said.
